title: Range Sum Query 2D - Mutable
description: Brute force to optimized: re-summing an entire rectangle on every query versus a 2D Fenwick tree balancing update and sumRegion to O(log rows times log cols).

blocks.text: Problem Summary: Given a 2D matrix, design a class supporting update(row, col, val), which sets matrix[row][col] to val, and sumRegion(row1, col1, row2, col2), which returns the sum of the rectangle with top-left corner (row1, col1) and bottom-right corner (row2, col2). Both operations can be called repeatedly, in any order.

blocks.text: This is the 2D version of Range Sum Query - Mutable: maintain a matrix that can be updated at a single cell at any time, while also answering "what is the sum of this rectangle" queries, both needing to stay efficient under repeated, interleaved calls.

blocks.title: Analogy: A Spreadsheet Supporting Fast Cell Edits and Fast Rectangular Totals
blocks.text: Picture a large spreadsheet where a single cell can be edited at any time, and a rectangular block of cells needs its total computed on demand. A 2D Fenwick tree organizes the sheet into overlapping partial rectangle sums, so both an edit and a rectangle total only ever touch a small number of entries.

blocks.caption: A 2D Fenwick tree: every update or query touches only a small number of cells

blocks.text: Summing rows 2 to 4 and columns 1 to 3 gives 8.
After changing the cell at (3,2) from 0 to 2, the same rectangle sum becomes 10.

Before choosing between a plain matrix (fast update, slow rectangle sum) or a plain 2D prefix sum matrix (fast sum, slow update), notice the 1D Fenwick tree idea from Range Sum Query - Mutable extends naturally into two dimensions.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: A plain matrix supports O(1) updates but O(rows times cols) rectangle sums.

Observation 2: A plain 2D prefix sum matrix supports O(1) rectangle sums but O(rows times cols) updates, since a change shifts every later prefix sum.

Observation 3: A 2D Fenwick tree splits each cell's contribution among O(log rows times log cols) partial-sum entries, so both an update and a prefix-sum query only touch that many entries.

Observation 4: A rectangle sum, sumRegion(r1, c1, r2, c2), is then the standard 2D inclusion-exclusion: prefix(r2,c2) minus prefix(r1-1,c2) minus prefix(r2,c1-1) plus prefix(r1-1,c1-1), each an O(log rows times log cols) query.
This leads to maintaining a 2D Fenwick tree: update adjusts it by the change in a cell's value, and sumRegion combines four 2D prefix queries via inclusion-exclusion.
Keep a plain matrix. On update, overwrite the cell directly. On sumRegion, add up every cell in the rectangle directly, from scratch.

items: Store the matrix as a plain 2D array.
update(row, col, val): set matrix[row][col] to val directly.
sumRegion(r1, c1, r2, c2): loop over every cell in the rectangle, summing directly.

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: update is trivially fast, a single write.
sumRegion recomputes the sum of the entire requested rectangle from scratch every single call.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(1) per update, O(rows times cols) per sumRegion in the worst case.
Space: O(rows times cols).
Limitation: if sumRegion is called often, or on large rectangles, repeatedly re-summing from scratch becomes the bottleneck.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text:
Why a plain matrix or a plain 2D prefix sum matrix is not enough: one makes updates fast at the cost of slow sums, the other flips the tradeoff entirely.

What structure balances both: a 2D Fenwick tree, splitting each cell's contribution among a logarithmic number of overlapping partial-sum entries in both dimensions.

The core idea: update by the DIFFERENCE between old and new cell values, and answer sumRegion with the standard 4-corner inclusion-exclusion over 2D prefix queries, each O(log rows times log cols).

Build a 2D Fenwick tree from the initial matrix. On update(row, col, val), compute the delta from the current value and add it into the tree at (row, col). On sumRegion(r1, c1, r2, c2), combine four 2D prefix queries via inclusion-exclusion: prefix(r2,c2) minus prefix(r1-1,c2) minus prefix(r2,c1-1) plus prefix(r1-1,c1-1).

blocks.caption: Optimized flow: 2D Fenwick tree, delta updates, 4-corner inclusion-exclusion queries

blocks.text: The 2D Fenwick tree structure guarantees that both an update and a prefix-sum query only touch O(log rows times log cols) entries, since each cell's value is folded into a logarithmic number of overlapping partial-sum ranges in both directions. Updating by the DIFFERENCE keeps the tree consistent without a rebuild, and any rectangle sum reduces to the standard 4-corner inclusion-exclusion over 2D prefix queries.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(log rows times log cols) per update and per sumRegion.
Space: O(rows times cols) for the 2D Fenwick tree.

blocks.text: Range Sum Query 2D - Mutable is the direct 2D extension of Range Sum Query - Mutable: the same delta-update and inclusion-exclusion ideas, just applied across two dimensions instead of one.

items: Forgetting the standard 2D inclusion-exclusion formula (add back the doubly-subtracted corner) when computing a rectangle sum from prefix queries.
Updating by the new value instead of the DELTA between old and new values.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: If the interviewer says "how does this differ from the 1D version", think: the same Fenwick tree idea, just indexed in two dimensions, with the standard 4-corner inclusion-exclusion for rectangle sums.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text: The brute force runs update in O(1) and sumRegion in O(rows times cols). The optimized 2D Fenwick tree runs both in O(log rows times log cols). Both use O(rows times cols) space.

items: Pattern: a 2D Fenwick tree, the direct extension of the 1D Range Sum Query - Mutable technique.
Core Idea: update by the delta between old and new cell values; answer a rectangle sum with the standard 4-corner inclusion-exclusion over 2D prefix queries.
Time: O(1) update / O(rows times cols) sumRegion for the brute force, O(log rows times log cols) for both in the optimized approach.
Most Important Observation: this is exactly the 1D Fenwick tree technique, extended dimension by dimension.
Interview Difficulty: a natural follow-up to the 1D version once that is understood.
One line memory trick: 2D Fenwick tree; update by the delta, query with 4-corner inclusion-exclusion.
